title: Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E420 is Euler's paper recasting the calculus of variations by embedding the varied object in a one-parameter family. On the previous page, z is made a function z(x,y,t) of the surface coordinates x, y and a new parameter t. At t = 0 it reproduces the given surface; infinitesimal t gives the neighbouring surfaces. Since x and y do not depend on t, the 'variation' is the partial differential in t alone.

This page (end of §19): for an expression V(x,y,z) of the 'first genus', with dV = L dx + M dy + N dz, the increment due to t alone is found by putting dx = dy = 0 and dz = dt(∂z/∂t). This gives dt(∂V/∂t) = N dt(∂z/∂t), hence ∂V/∂t = N ∂z/∂t. In modern terms, δV = V_z δz with δ = ∂/∂t at t = 0. Such expressions again form the first genus.

§20 begins the 'second genus': expressions V that involve, besides x, y, z, the derivatives of z. Ignoring t for the moment, z has two kinds of increments (from x and from y). Euler fixes an indexed notation:
- first order: p = ∂z/∂x, p' = ∂z/∂y;
- second order: q = z_xx, q' = z_xy, q'' = z_yy;
- third order: r = z_xxx, r' = z_xxy, r'' = z_xyy, r''' = z_yyy.
He records the compatibility relations ∂p/∂x = q, ∂p/∂y = ∂p'/∂x = q', ∂p'/∂y = q''. These encode equality of mixed partials, and the next page continues them to third and fourth order. The purpose is to set up the general differential dV = L dx + M dy + N dz + P dp + P' dp' + Q dq + …, then compute δV and integrate by parts in double integrals, giving the Euler–Lagrange (Euler–Ostrogradsky) equation for surfaces.

ideas.what: Variation as partial derivative with respect to an auxiliary family parameter t, with x and y held fixed; δV = N δz for V = V(x,y,z)
ideas.modern_name: First variation via one-parameter families (Gateaux derivative at t = 0)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E420 and the companion papers E385/E386 on the parameter method, c. 1771), following Lagrange's δ-algorithm
ideas.where_published: E420 itself; also E385/E386 and the supplement on variations in Institutiones calculi integralis vol. 3

ideas.what: Indexed letters p, p'; q, q', q''; r, … for partial derivatives of z(x,y), with relations expressing symmetry of mixed partials
ideas.modern_name: Jet-coordinate notation for partial derivatives (cf. Monge's p, q, r, s, t)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Institutiones calculi integralis vol. 3, 1770, uses p, q, r, s, t); later standardized by Monge and Lagrange

deep.surprise_reason: Purely notational and set-up material: the variation of a function of z, and a naming scheme for partial derivatives up to third order. It is well known as part of Euler's 1770s treatment of double-integral variational problems.
transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially faithful to the image. Note the inconsistency in the original: §20 prints lowercase italic 'v' for the expression where V is used elsewhere (§19, §21).
